day_by_day.morning: Arrival — Flight AC lands at 13:00, so no morning activities. Use this time to rest on the plane and review your Montreal plans.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check in to your Old Montreal accommodation, then take a self-guided stroll through Vieux-Montréal. Wander the iconic cobblestone streets, admire the architecture of Place Jacques-Cartier, and peek at the exterior of Notre-Dame Basilica (free from outside). Get oriented with your neighbourhood and pick up a free tourist map from the hotel or a nearby info kiosk.
day_by_day.evening: Head to the Montreal Jazz Festival Street Performances at the Quartier des Spectacles (a short walk or cheap metro ride from Old Montreal). Hundreds of free outdoor concerts run throughout the festival — grab a spot on the plaza, enjoy world-class live music under the summer sky, and soak up the electric festival atmosphere at no cost.

meals.breakfast: Eat on the plane or grab a quick snack at the airport upon arrival.
meals.lunch: Pick up a fresh baguette sandwich or a crêpe from a street vendor near Place Jacques-Cartier (~$8–12 CAD) after check-in.
meals.dinner: Grab a classic poutine from La Banquise's Old Montreal-area competitors or a nearby casse-croûte (Québécois diner) for ~$12–15 CAD before heading to the Jazz Festival. Many food trucks and affordable vendors also line the festival grounds.

day_by_day.notes: The Montreal Jazz Festival typically runs late June through early July — confirm 2027 exact dates in advance. If the festival has ended, the Quartier des Spectacles still has free public art installations and a lively evening scene. Metro Day Pass (~$11 CAD) is great value if you plan multiple rides.

day_by_day.morning: Old Montreal Historic Walking Tour — Start your morning with a deep dive into Vieux-Montréal. Visit the stunning Notre-Dame Basilica interior (entry ~$15 CAD — worth every penny for the jaw-dropping Gothic Revival interior). Then explore Place d'Armes, Pointe-à-Callière archaeology museum exterior, and the Old Port waterfront. A self-guided walk costs almost nothing beyond the basilica entry.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take the metro (Line 2 Orange) north to the Jean-Talon Market Food Tour. Explore one of North America's largest open-air markets — sample free tastings of local Quebec cheeses, maple products, fresh berries, and charcuterie from vendors. Buy a small picnic spread of cheese, bread, and fruit for a very affordable lunch right at the market.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the Jazz Festival Street Performances for another evening of free world-class outdoor concerts. Arrive early to claim a good viewing spot on the main outdoor stages. Browse the festival atmosphere, enjoy street performers, and mingle with locals.

meals.breakfast: Café au lait and a buttery croissant or pain au chocolat from a local boulangerie in Old Montreal (~$6–9 CAD). Try Olive + Gourmando or a neighbourhood bakery.
meals.lunch: DIY picnic at Jean-Talon Market — assemble a spread of Quebec cheese, fresh bread, seasonal fruit, and a maple treat for ~$10–14 CAD total.
meals.dinner: Grab affordable eats from food stalls near the Jazz Festival grounds, or stop at a BYOB (apportez votre vin) restaurant on nearby Rue Saint-Denis for a budget-friendly Québécois meal (~$15–20 CAD for food; bring your own wine from a dépanneur to save on drinks).

day_by_day.notes: Jean-Talon Market is open daily in summer, typically 7am–6pm. Metro fare is ~$3.75 CAD per ride or use a day pass. BYOB restaurants are a uniquely Montréal budget hack — buy wine at a corner store (dépanneur) for $12–15 CAD and bring it to a licensed BYOB restaurant to save significantly on your bill.

day_by_day.morning: Plateau Mont-Royal Food Crawl — Take the metro to the Plateau neighbourhood and spend your morning exploring one of Montreal's most vibrant and culturally rich areas. Browse the colourful Victorian row houses, murals, and independent boutiques along Avenue du Mont-Royal and Rue Saint-Laurent. Visit the Marché du Plateau or a local café to start the day.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the Plateau Mont-Royal Food Crawl in earnest — sample iconic local dishes including classic poutine (try La Banquise, open 24/7, ~$12–16 CAD), a Montreal-style bagel from Fairmount Bagel or St-Viateur Bagel (freshly baked, ~$1–2 each), and smoked meat from a deli. Finish with a stroll through Parc Lafontaine — a beautiful free green space perfect for people-watching on a warm summer afternoon.
day_by_day.evening: Head back toward the Quartier des Spectacles for a final evening at the Montreal Jazz Festival Street Performances, or explore the free outdoor cultural events and pop-up performances that are common throughout Montreal in July. Check local listings (MTL.org) for any free neighbourhood festivals or outdoor cinema events happening this evening.

meals.breakfast: Fresh Montreal bagel with cream cheese from Fairmount Bagel or St-Viateur Bagel (~$3–5 CAD) eaten while walking — an authentic local experience.
meals.lunch: Classic poutine at La Banquise (~$12–16 CAD) — a Montreal institution. Split a large portion if travelling with a companion.
meals.dinner: BYOB Plateau restaurant or a hearty meal at a Vietnamese or Lebanese restaurant on Boulevard Saint-Laurent (Montreal's 'Main' street has incredible affordable ethnic food for ~$12–18 CAD).

day_by_day.notes: The Plateau is very walkable and bikeable. BIXI bike share (~$7 CAD for a 24-hour pass) is an excellent and fun way to explore the neighbourhood. Parc Lafontaine is free and beautiful — great for a mid-afternoon rest in the shade. Friday evenings in summer often have extra street activity and pop-up events.

day_by_day.morning: Return to the Old Montreal waterfront and explore the Old Port (Vieux-Port) area in the morning light. Walk along the waterfront promenade, visit the Clock Tower (Tour de l'Horloge — free to climb for panoramic views), and browse the weekend artisan market stalls that pop up along the port on summer Saturdays.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit Mont Royal Park (Parc du Mont-Royal) — take the metro to Mont-Royal station and hike or walk up to the Kondiaronk Belvedere lookout for a stunning free panoramic view of the entire city. This is one of the most iconic Montreal experiences and costs nothing. Pack snacks from a nearby dépanneur for a picnic at the summit.
day_by_day.evening: Final evening — return to the Quartier des Spectacles or Old Montreal for a farewell dinner and a last walk through the neighbourhood. Browse souvenir shops along Rue Saint-Paul (Old Montreal's main shopping street) for affordable local gifts like maple candy, Quebec craft products, or local art prints.

meals.breakfast: Full Québécois breakfast at a local greasy spoon (casse-croûte) near Old Montreal — eggs, toast, beans, and café au lait for ~$10–13 CAD. Look for 'déjeuner spécial' specials on chalkboard signs.
meals.lunch: Picnic on Mont Royal — grab supplies from a dépanneur or Jean-Coutu pharmacy: sandwiches, chips, drinks, and a maple cookie for ~$10–12 CAD total.
meals.dinner: Splurge slightly on your last night — try a classic Québécois restaurant in Old Montreal for tourtière, maple-glazed duck, or a hearty soupe à l'oignon. Look for table d'hôte (prix-fixe) menus which offer great value at ~$20–28 CAD for a multi-course meal.

day_by_day.notes: Mont Royal Park is free and open daily — the hike to the belvedere takes about 20–30 minutes at a leisurely pace. Wear comfortable shoes. If you have an early departure on Day 5, pack your bags the night before and confirm checkout time with your accommodation. The 747 express bus connects downtown to Trudeau Airport (~$11 CAD, 24-hour service) — a very budget-friendly airport transfer option.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival & Hotel Check-In — Flight AC lands at 13:00, so the morning is in transit. Take the 747 express bus or a rideshare from Trudeau Airport to your Old Montreal hotel (~35–45 min). Check in, freshen up, and orient yourself with a quick walk around the cobblestone streets near your accommodation.
day_by_day.afternoon: Old Montreal Historic Walking Tour — Starting from your hotel, join or self-guide a walking tour of Vieux-Montréal. Visit the breathtaking Notre-Dame Basilica (book a timed entry ticket in advance, ~$15 CAD), stroll Place Jacques-Cartier, admire the Bonsecours Market facade, and soak in the historic architecture along Rue Saint-Paul. The neighbourhood is steps from your hotel, making this the perfect low-effort first afternoon.
day_by_day.evening: Montreal Jazz Festival Street Performances — Head to the Quartier des Spectacles (a short walk or 10-min rideshare from Old Montreal) to catch free outdoor Jazz Festival performances. The festival runs nightly with multiple outdoor stages featuring world-class artists at no cost. Grab a cold drink from a festival vendor and enjoy the electric summer atmosphere.

meals.breakfast: Grab a coffee and croissant at the airport or a café near the hotel upon arrival — try Crew Collective & Café in Old Montreal for a stunning setting (~$10–15 CAD).
meals.lunch: Pick up a quick bite after check-in at Olive & Gourmando on Rue Saint-Paul — a beloved Old Montreal deli known for sandwiches and fresh salads (~$18–25 CAD).
meals.dinner: Dine at L'Orignal on Rue Saint-Paul Est — a mid-range Quebec-focused bistro serving charcuterie, local cheeses, and seasonal dishes in a warm, rustic setting (~$40–55 CAD per person with drinks).

day_by_day.notes: Since arrival is at 13:00, keep Day 1 relaxed and geographically close to the hotel. Notre-Dame Basilica tickets sell out — book online before your trip. The Jazz Festival outdoor stages are free; only ticketed indoor shows require purchase. Comfortable walking shoes are essential on the cobblestones.

day_by_day.morning: Jean-Talon Market Food Tour — Take the Metro Orange Line north to Jean-Talon station (~25 min from Old Montreal). Spend the morning exploring one of North America's largest open-air markets. Sample local Quebec cheeses, fresh maple products, artisan charcuterie, seasonal fruits, and freshly baked goods. Chat with local vendors and pick up snacks for later. Arrive by 9:00–9:30 AM for the best experience before the midday crowds.
day_by_day.afternoon: Plateau Mont-Royal Food Crawl — Walk or take the Metro one stop to the Plateau neighbourhood. Spend the afternoon on a self-guided food crawl: try classic poutine at La Banquise (open 24/7, iconic), grab a Montreal-style bagel from Fairmount Bagel or St-Viateur Bagel, and explore the colourful murals and boutiques along Avenue Mont-Royal. This neighbourhood perfectly captures Montreal's creative, local character.
day_by_day.evening: Montreal Jazz Festival — Return downtown to the Quartier des Spectacles for another evening of Jazz Festival performances. Tonight, consider splurging on a ticketed indoor show at one of the festival venues (tickets ~$30–80 CAD depending on the artist) for a more intimate concert experience, or enjoy the free outdoor mainstage headliner.

meals.breakfast: Eat at the Jean-Talon Market itself — grab a fresh pastry and coffee from one of the market's café stalls (~$8–12 CAD). This IS the morning activity.
meals.lunch: Poutine and a Montreal bagel during the Plateau food crawl. La Banquise poutine runs ~$14–18 CAD; a bagel with cream cheese at Fairmount is ~$4–6 CAD.
meals.dinner: Try Au Pied de Cochon's more casual neighbour, or dine at Damas Restaurant on Avenue Laurier for upscale Syrian-Mediterranean cuisine with Quebec ingredients — a true Montreal fusion experience (~$45–65 CAD per person).

day_by_day.notes: Jean-Talon Market is best on weekday mornings — less crowded than weekends. Bring a small tote bag for market purchases. The Plateau is very walkable; rent a BIXI bike (Montreal's bike-share, ~$6.50/30 min) to cruise between food stops. Check the Jazz Festival schedule at montrealjazzfest.com for the evening's lineup.

day_by_day.morning: Montreal Museum of Fine Arts — Take the Metro to Guy-Concordia station and walk to Canada's most visited art museum. Spend the morning exploring the permanent collection spanning ancient to contemporary art, plus any special summer exhibitions. Friday mornings are relatively quiet. General admission is ~$24 CAD; permanent collection is free on select days — check their website.
day_by_day.afternoon: Mile End & Cultural Exploration — After the museum, walk or take the Metro to the Mile End neighbourhood, Montreal's creative hub. Visit the iconic Saint-Viateur bagel shop, browse independent bookstores and vinyl record shops, explore street art along Rue Bernard, and pop into local boutiques. Stop by Parc Sir-Wilfrid-Laurier for a rest and people-watching in true Montreal fashion.
day_by_day.evening: Jazz Festival Grand Finale Evening — Friday night at the Jazz Festival is one of the busiest and most exciting nights, with major outdoor mainstage performances and a festive crowd. Head back to the Quartier des Spectacles early (by 7:00 PM) to claim a good viewing spot. The outdoor shows are free and the energy on a Friday night is unmatched. Grab festival food and drinks from nearby vendors.

meals.breakfast: Start the day at Café Parvis near the museum district — a stylish café with excellent espresso and avocado toast or pastries (~$12–18 CAD).
meals.lunch: Grab lunch in the museum's Café des Beaux-Arts or head to Maison Boulud at the Ritz-Carlton for a mid-range lunch prix-fixe (~$35–45 CAD) — a treat worth the splurge on a balanced budget.
meals.dinner: Eat before the Jazz Festival at Schwartz's Deli on Boulevard Saint-Laurent — the legendary Montreal smoked meat sandwich institution. Expect a short queue; it's worth it (~$20–28 CAD with sides and a drink).

day_by_day.notes: The Museum of Fine Arts is closed on Mondays but open all day Friday. Book museum tickets online to avoid queues. Mile End and the Plateau are very walkable from each other. Friday night Jazz Festival crowds are large — arrive early for outdoor stages. The warm 25°C summer weather makes evening festival-going very pleasant; bring a light layer for after dark.

day_by_day.morning: Mount Royal Park — Start your final morning with a walk or hike up Mont Royal, the iconic hill at the heart of the city. Take the Chemin Olmsted trail to the Kondiaronk Belvedere lookout for a panoramic view of Montreal's skyline and the St. Lawrence River. Rent a BIXI bike at the base for a scenic ride around the park. This is a beloved local ritual and perfectly captures Montreal's outdoor culture.
day_by_day.afternoon: Old Montreal & Departure Prep — Return to your hotel neighbourhood for a leisurely final afternoon. Browse the boutiques and galleries along Rue Notre-Dame and Rue Saint-Paul, visit the Marché Bonsecours interior for local artisan crafts and souvenirs, and take a final stroll along the Old Port waterfront (Vieux-Port). The St. Lawrence River views and the old stone buildings make for perfect last memories of the city.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell Dinner in Old Montreal — End your Montreal trip with a memorable dinner close to the hotel. Celebrate the trip with a proper Quebec-inspired meal featuring local ingredients and classic dishes.

meals.breakfast: Pick up fresh bagels and coffee from a local bakery near the hotel before heading to Mont Royal — try Café Névé in the Plateau for excellent espresso and baked goods (~$10–14 CAD).
meals.lunch: Enjoy a relaxed lunch at Terrasse Place d'Armes in Old Montreal — a rooftop terrace restaurant with great views and a solid mid-range menu of Quebec classics (~$25–38 CAD).
meals.dinner: Farewell dinner at Garde Manger on Rue Saint-François-Xavier — a celebrated Old Montreal restaurant by celebrity chef Chuck Hughes, known for creative seafood and local ingredients in a lively atmosphere (~$55–75 CAD per person with drinks). Reserve in advance, especially for a Saturday.

day_by_day.notes: Mont Royal is free and accessible by foot, BIXI bike, or bus (Route 11). Wear comfortable shoes for the uphill trail. Saturday is a great day for the Old Port area — there are often street performers and artisan markets. Marché Bonsecours artisan vendors are a great spot for authentic Quebec souvenirs (maple products, local art, Inuit crafts). Confirm your checkout time with the hotel and arrange airport transport in advance — allow 60–75 minutes to get to Trudeau Airport on a Saturday.

The tour runs approximately 2.5 hours and is easily accessible on foot from your hotel.

meals.breakfast: Not applicable — mid-day arrival. Grab a light snack or café au lait at Crew Collective & Café near the hotel upon settling in.
meals.lunch: Olive & Gourmando (Vieux-Montréal): A beloved Old Montreal institution known for artisanal sandwiches, fresh salads, and house-baked pastries. Perfect for a relaxed first meal after arrival.
meals.dinner: Toqué! — Montreal's legendary flagship fine-dining restaurant by chef Normand Laprise. Celebrates Quebec's finest seasonal ingredients with an exquisite tasting menu. Reserve well in advance. Expect an exceptional wine pairing experience.

day_by_day.notes: Arrange private airport transfer in advance for a seamless luxury arrival. Book Notre-Dame Basilica's AURA experience tickets online before the trip. Toqué! reservations are essential — book 4–6 weeks ahead. Weather should be warm (~25°C); light layers recommended for the evening festival.

day_by_day.morning: Jean-Talon Market Food Tour: Take a private car or rideshare to the iconic Jean-Talon Market in the Mile End district — one of North America's largest and most celebrated open-air markets. Join a premium guided food tour sampling artisanal Quebec cheeses, freshly tapped maple products, charcuterie, heirloom vegetables, and local pastries. Interact with passionate vendors and discover the heart of Quebec's culinary identity.
day_by_day.afternoon: Montreal Museum of Fine Arts Visit: Head to Canada's most visited art museum on Sherbrooke Street. Explore the impressive permanent collection spanning ancient civilizations to contemporary art, as well as any special summer exhibitions. Consider booking a private docent-led tour for a more curated, in-depth experience through the galleries.
day_by_day.evening: Plateau Mont-Royal Food Crawl: Spend the early evening exploring Montreal's hippest and most characterful neighborhood. Sample iconic local dishes including classic poutine (La Banquise style), Montreal-style smoked meat, fresh bagels from St-Viateur, and locally crafted ice cream. Conclude with cocktails at a rooftop bar on the Plateau.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at your hotel or at Café Parvis nearby — known for excellent espresso, avocado toast, and house-baked goods in an elegant, airy setting.
meals.lunch: Chez Victoire (Plateau Mont-Royal): A chic French-inspired bistro with a superb weekend brunch and lunch menu. Beautifully plated seasonal dishes with a curated natural wine list.
meals.dinner: Le Filet: An intimate, seafood-forward gem on Mont-Royal Avenue with a creative, market-driven menu. Renowned for its refined small plates, exceptional raw bar, and outstanding natural wine selection. Perfect cap to a food-focused day.

day_by_day.notes: Jean-Talon Market is best experienced early — aim to arrive by 9:00–9:30 AM. Book a premium guided market tour through a local culinary tour operator (e.g., MTL Gourmet or Tastes of Montreal). The Museum of Fine Arts offers a premium membership or guided experience worth upgrading to. Comfortable walking shoes are essential for the Plateau food crawl.

day_by_day.morning: Montreal Museum of Fine Arts — Special Exhibition Deep Dive (if not fully explored on Day 2) OR a private guided art and architecture walk through the Golden Square Mile neighborhood, exploring Montreal's Gilded Age mansions, heritage churches, and cultural landmarks along Sherbrooke Street West. This walk reveals the city's English-speaking elite history and stunning Beaux-Arts architecture.
day_by_day.afternoon: Montreal Jazz Festival — Ticketed Indoor Concert Experience: The Jazz Festival runs premium indoor ticketed concerts at Maison symphonique de Montréal and Salle Wilfrid-Pelletier. Secure tickets to an afternoon or early-evening headline performance by a world-class jazz or crossover artist. This is the premium festival experience beyond the free outdoor stages.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the Quartier des Spectacles for the Jazz Festival's Friday night peak atmosphere — outdoor main stage headliner performance, festival food and craft cocktail vendors, and an unforgettable open-air concert experience with thousands of music lovers in the heart of the city.

meals.breakfast: In-hotel breakfast or a visit to Foxy (Mile End) — a sophisticated all-day café serving beautifully crafted breakfast plates, house-made granola, smoked salmon, and specialty coffee in a bright, design-forward space.
meals.lunch: Maison Boulud at the Ritz-Carlton Montreal: Michelin-caliber French cuisine by Daniel Boulud in one of Montreal's most iconic luxury hotels. The garden terrace is magnificent in summer. A perfect leisurely luxury lunch.
meals.dinner: Racines: An acclaimed wine bar and restaurant in the Quartier des Spectacles area, ideal for pre- or post-concert dining. Outstanding natural wine list, elevated small plates, and charcuterie boards. Perfectly positioned for the Jazz Festival evening.

day_by_day.notes: Jazz Festival indoor concert tickets sell out quickly — book as early as possible through the official festival website (montrealjazzfest.com). Friday night is one of the busiest festival nights; arrive at outdoor stages early for a good viewing spot. Maison Boulud lunch reservations recommended. The weather should remain warm — ideal for outdoor evening concerts.

day_by_day.morning: Mount Royal Park Morning Experience: Take a private car to the base of Mount Royal and enjoy a guided or self-directed walk up to the Kondiaronk Belvedere lookout for panoramic views over Montreal's skyline and the St. Lawrence River. Rent a rowboat on Beaver Lake or simply enjoy a peaceful morning picnic in the park — the lungs of the city designed by Frederick Law Olmsted.
day_by_day.afternoon: Plateau Mont-Royal & Mile End Neighborhood Exploration: Spend the afternoon wandering the colorful streets of the Plateau and Mile End at a relaxed pace. Visit independent boutiques, local art galleries, and murals. Stop at the legendary St-Viateur Bagel shop for a fresh-from-the-wood-oven Montreal bagel. Browse the record shops and bookstores that define this bohemian neighborhood's creative character.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell Dinner & Jazz Festival Grand Finale: Enjoy a spectacular farewell dinner before heading to the Jazz Festival for one final evening of world-class music. Saturday night features the festival's biggest outdoor headliner performances — a truly unforgettable send-off to your Montreal experience.

meals.breakfast: Arthurs Nosh Bar (Mile End): A beloved Jewish-inspired brunch spot with exceptional smoked salmon platters, latkes, shakshuka, and house-made pastries. Quintessential Montreal morning dining.
meals.lunch: Fairmount Bagel + picnic provisions from a nearby deli or épicerie fine — assemble a gourmet picnic to enjoy in Mount Royal Park or on a Plateau terrace. Include local cheeses, charcuterie, and a bottle of Quebec cider.
meals.dinner: Monarque: One of Montreal's most celebrated fine-dining restaurants in Old Montreal, offering a sophisticated French-Québécois tasting menu in a stunning heritage space. Chef Marc-André Jetté's seasonal menu showcases the very best of Quebec's summer bounty. An exceptional farewell dinner. Full wine pairing highly recommended.

day_by_day.notes: Mount Royal Park is easily accessible by rideshare or taxi from Old Montreal. Bring sunscreen and water for the park walk. Monarque reservations are essential — book at least 3–4 weeks in advance and request a window or heritage-room table for atmosphere. Saturday is the Jazz Festival's biggest night — arrive early to the Quartier des Spectacles for premium positioning at the main outdoor stage. Consider arranging a private car for the evening to move seamlessly between dinner and the festival.
